tools.name: browser_context
tools.description: Open or close a browser for this agent. "fresh" starts with an empty throwaway profile and uses the legacy CLI outside copied-profile protection. "mine" makes a private Edge/Chrome copy without saved-login stores or linked files, retaining qualified single-link cookie/encryption metadata. Its owned native producer hides all input/textarea/editable and unknown-region values, refuses raw commands, and reads the page with its child frames (same-process and out-of-process) and acts on refs anywhere in them. Both run in the background without touching the person's open windows. A failed mine open never authorizes computer control, attaching to the person's browser, interactive sign-in, or switching identity/transport to bypass a refusal. COPY_SOURCE_PERMISSION means OS access was refused, not that Desk can grant it; COPY_SOURCE_POLICY means source qualification failed. Continue independent work; fresh has no inherited sign-in and is not an authenticated substitute. Keep contextId, and close when done; closing deletes the private folder.

action.description: open starts a new browser and returns its contextId; close shuts it and deletes its folder.

browser.description: open only. fresh: initially empty legacy profile. mine: protected private copy with restricted native output/actions, deleted on close. Defaults to fresh.

contextId.description: close only. The contextId that open returned.

tools.name: browser_command
tools.description: Run a command in an owned browser context. args is a list of literal strings, never shell or user JavaScript. Start with ["goto","https://example.com"] or ["snapshot"], then use current refs with click/fill/type/press/select/check/uncheck/hover. In mine the commands are: snapshot [--interactive|--save], find <text>, goto <url>, go-back, go-forward, reload, wait [<seconds>|<text>|--gone <text>], click/dblclick/hover/check/uncheck <ref>, fill/type <ref> <text>, press [<ref>] <key>, select <ref> <value>, mousewheel <dx> <dy>, resize <w> <h>, screenshot [<ref>] [--full], tab-list, tab-new, tab-select <n>, tab-close [<n>]. Use ["wait","<text you expect>"] while a page loads (it returns a snapshot); eval is never needed. A snapshot reads only what the page shows, compactly (unnamed wrappers are left out), and stays short: on a long page it keeps controls and named lines, then text in page order, says how many lines it left out, and [\"find\",\"<text>\"] shows just the lines holding that text with their refs. A page that keeps changing is fine: act on a ref soon after the snapshot, and if it reports AUTH_SNAPSHOT_INVALIDATED, snapshot again. To type into a rich-text editor, fill its textbox ref, then press Enter on that ref or ["press","Enter"]; typed.verified says whether it holds the text. A transient error page: ["reload"], then wait. Every refusal says what to do instead. In mine, owned native output always redacts protected values; eval/run-code/raw storage/network/console and PDF exports are refused. screenshot saves a PNG of the tab or one ref in the context's files folder and returns its path; every input, textarea and editable region is masked in it, in every frame, as a snapshot redacts them; a page with a closed shadow, or a child frame that fails to read, is refused. ["snapshot","--save"] writes only a sanitized owner-named JSON artifact; raw/JSON/filename opt-outs are unavailable. Child frames show their content inside a frame node, scrubbed of every value typed anywhere in the tab; a frame that cannot be read at that moment shows empty and framesOmitted counts it. Closed shadows and refs whose element changed are refused; an action may have applied before post-action output fails. Fresh retains legacy CLI commands outside the copied-profile boundary. Open/close only through browser_context.

contextId.description: The contextId that browser_context open returned.

args.description: The command and its arguments, for example ["snapshot"] or ["fill","e4","text"].
